Interesting! After clicking at (47, 38):
- Blue pixels went from 81 to 88 (+7) - liquid was added back!
- Container center: row=28.3, col=30.2
- Container is now at rows 23-34, cols 23-37
- Only 35 cells changed (much less than before)
- Blue pixels in bottom container: 0
Wait, blue pixels INCREASED from 81 to 88. That's +7. But I didn't use ACTION7. So either:
1. The container refilled itself somehow
2. The liquid that was spilling got recaptured
Looking at the container position: it moved from rows 11-21, cols 22-37 to rows 23-34, cols 23-37. It moved DOWN and slightly RIGHT. The click was at (47, 38), which is below and slightly right of the container. So the container moved toward the click point, as expected.
But the blue pixels increased! This is strange. Unless the liquid that was "spilling" (outside the container walls) got recaptured when the container moved to a more upright position.
Actually, looking at the container orientation: previously it was tilted with the opening facing down-right. Now it's more upright (the blue pixels form a more rectangular shape). When the container is more upright, it can hold more liquid without spilling.
So the mechanic seems to be:
1. Clicking causes the container to move toward the click point
2. The container also rotates based on the click position
3. When the container is tilted, liquid spills out (blue pixels decrease)
4. When the container is more upright, it can hold more liquid (blue pixels increase)
5. ACTION7 refills the container to full
The container is now at rows 23-34, cols 23-37, which is closer to the bottom container (rows 38-57, cols 30-47). The horizontal alignment is better (cols 23-37 vs 30-47, overlapping at cols 30-37).
Let me keep clicking below the container to move it down toward the bottom container. I'll click at (47, 38) again to continue moving it down.
